articles.title: Watchdog demands apology after UN memorial erroneously honors Hamas terrorist
articles.summary: UN Watch says UNRWA teacher Imad Youssif El Samhouri glorified terrorism for years before the United Nations honored him at a memorial service.
articles.body: A solemn candle-lighting ceremony honoring United Nations employees who died in 2025 while working for the world body has sparked criticism after it unwittingly named an employee who was later revealed to be a Hamas commander. At the annual memorial service in June honoring 136 employees who died in service to the U.N. in 2025, Secretary-General António Guterres, General Assembly President Annalena Baerbock, and then-Security Council President Leonor Zalabata Torres helped light a candle representing "an eternal flame." An official later read Imad Youssif El Samhouri’s name alongside those of other U.N. employees as a violinist played somber music. El Samhouri was employed by the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East (UNRWA) as a teacher and associate principal before becoming principal of UNRWA Rafah Preparatory Boys School B. On Aug. 8, Hamas identified El Samhouri through messaging site Telegram as a field commander in the Al-Qassam Brigades. UN CHIEF BACKS OFFICIAL WHO REPOSTED ANTI-ISRAEL ACTIVIST'S CLAIMS AMID CALLS FOR INVESTIGATION During the event, Guterres said that "more U.N. colleagues have been killed in Gaza than in any other conflict or disaster in the history of the United Nations. Some died alongside their families, in their homes, in the places they sought refuge. Others were killed while carrying out their duties in offices, in shelters, and in communities they served. These tragedies weigh heavily on us all and should be remembered by the entire world. Let me be clear. U.N. personnel must never be targeted." Guterres also said, "In keeping with long-standing practice, we have sought the consent of families to read aloud the names of those we honor. Tragically, in the case of men who served with UNRWA, we could not reach those families because they, too, have been killed or forced to flee." Hillel Neuer, executive director of UN Watch, has written an open letter to Guterres and Baerbock asking both to issue an apology for the incident and acknowledge that UNRWA is "unwilling or unable" to roust terrorists from its schools. Stéphane Dujarric, spokesperson for Guterres, told Fox News Digital during a press briefing last week, "[UNRWA] and we are always very deeply concerned when allegations against the former staff is raised. Obviously, when his name was included, the agency was not aware. I will remind you that the list of all UNRWA staff is shared with the Israeli parties as they are every year. His name was shared in the list of 2024. No concerns were raised based on that information from the Israeli side, and obviously, had those allegations been raised before, his name would likely not have been included." When pressed further about whether Guterres would retract the honors or issue an apology, Dujarric seemed to put the blame on Israel, "We're now stating our position, which makes it clear. Had we known, and had we been told, his name would probably not have been included." Israel’s U.N. Ambassador Danny Danon told Fox News Digital, "It is outrageous to watch the U.N. spokesperson struggle to clearly condemn the crimes committed by former UNRWA employees. Israel repeatedly warned the U.N. that active Hamas terrorists were operating within UNRWA and played a significant role in the atrocities of Oct. 7. The U.N. spokesperson’s response reflects Secretary-General Guterres’ entire tenure: the organization has lost its moral compass. It is because of terrorists like Imad Youssif El Samhouri and others that Israel ended UNRWA’s operations in Israel." Neuer has accumulated multiple social media posts that he says are attributed to El Samhouri, which demonstrate his support of so-called Palestinian martyrs, his praise for the kidnapping of Israeli teens, and his support for the "good news" of Hamas attacks between 2012 and 2014. El Samhouri’s case is one of about 200 cases that senior fellow at UN Watch Salo Aizenberg told Fox News Digital he has cataloged in which terror groups shared posthumous proof that journalists, NGO personnel, aid workers, lawyers and medical personnel were part of their organizations. Citing the Institute for Palestine Studies, which says El Samhouri was killed June 8, 2025, when Israeli forces targeted his tent with no warning, Aizenberg noted on X that El Samhouri was "using the cover of the humanitarian zone as a human shield" when he was targeted. ISRAEL ACCUSES UN OF PLACING IT ON SAME SEXUAL VIOLENCE BLACKLIST AS HAMAS TERRORISTS, SEVERS TIES In a martyr video viewed by Fox News Digital that the Israel Defense Forces provided, El Samhouri stands before multiple grenades and a weapon and states that "the call to arms has resounded in the hearts of the faithful and they have answered the call." He also says that "we have chosen jihad as our path; our anthem is that Death in the cause of Allah is our highest aspiration, and our resolve will not waver, no matter how long the road or how great the sacrifices." In the same video, while standing within what appears to be an underground tunnel, El Samhouri thanks God, "who has honored us with the tunnels and made them a means of resistance, a means by which the Zionist enemy never imagines we will emerge from beneath the ground." Neuer told Fox News Digital, "Samhouri publicly glorified terrorism, circulated Hamas battlefield propaganda and brought Hamas officials into UNRWA school life. Photographs show his own principal, Muhammad Al-Bardawil, repeatedly appearing at school events with Jumaa Al-Ghoul, Hamas’ representative in Rafah." He said, "The evidence shows clearly that many officials in the UNRWA school system knew about Samhouri’s support for terrorism and ties to Hamas, and that they actually tolerated or even encouraged it." TRUMP ADMINISTRATION TOUTS MORE THAN $1B IN UN BUDGET CUTS AS REFORM PUSH GAINS MOMENTUM El Samhouri is far from the first UNRWA employee exposed for support of Hamas. Neuer added that "in UN Watch's network map of more than 400 UNRWA employees, Hamas terrorists and their supporters have served as school principals, teachers and leaders of UNRWA’s powerful staff unions. Hamas influences UNRWA hiring and promotions, mobilizes strikes to protect extremists and intimidates international managers whenever even mild disciplinary action is attempted. Hamas pays some of its agents by getting them hired by UNRWA." According to Neuer, "The deeper problem is that the international leadership of UNRWA and of the U.N. rarely act. This is hardly a vetting oversight — it's a system failure. UNRWA has demonstrated that it is either unwilling or unable to remove Hamas terrorists from its schools. UNRWA cannot be reformed; it must be dismantled if Gaza is ever to be deradicalized and given a real future for peace and success." ISRAELI AMBASSADOR, UN OFFICIAL SHOUT OVER EACH OTHER IN TENSE EXCHANGE OVER SEXUAL VIOLENCE BLACKLIST UNRWA did not respond to Fox News Digital’s questions about El Samhouri’s social media activities, or whether his employment with the agency was further proof of its infiltration by Hamas. The USAID Office of Inspector General is currently investigating 1,500 UNRWA employees for possible ties to Hamas. Thus far, the USAID OIG has referred 108 UNRWA staff to the State Department, requesting they be suspended or barred from further cooperation with organizations that receive U.S. funding. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP A senior State Department official told Fox News Digital that "USAID OIG’s independent and ongoing investigation is revealing the pervasive extent to which UNRWA has aided and abetted Hamas. The investigation demonstrates that UNRWA hired droves of Hamas-linked terrorists and turned over their infrastructure to the terrorist group." The official stated, "This can never happen again, and other U.N. agencies would be wise to study the USAID OIG’s ongoing work to understand how to avoid a repeat."

articles.title: Teen planned middle school massacre before making deadly ‘last-minute choice’ to kill mom: official
articles.summary: Lilyana Wagner, 16, pleaded guilty to killing her mother after abandoning plans for a school shooting, listing six shooters in her confession.
articles.body: A teenage Georgia girl was convicted of brutally killing her mother after abandoning a plan to commit a school shooting, following an obsession with mass casualty events, authorities said. Lilyana Rose Wagner, 16, was sentenced to life in prison after pleading guilty to murder and aggravated assault in the November 2024 death of her mother Rachel Wagner, 51, Tifton District Attorney Patrick Warren said Tuesday. The slaying was discovered after Wagner, then 14, crashed her mother's car. Wagner told responding officers that she lived alone with her mother. The officers went to the home to perform a welfare check and discovered Rachel Wagner, who had not shown up for work and wasn't answering her phone, dead from a gunshot wound to the back of her head. GEORGIA HIGH SCHOOL SHOOTING SUSPECT COLT GRAY CHANGES PLEA TO GUILTY, NOW FACES LIFE IN PRISON Investigators found that the teenage Wagner had become obsessed with school shooters and mass shootings, developing an online and social media reputation as someone interested in planning and executing a mass casualty event. In a handwritten confession, the teen described the decision to kill her mother instead. "This whole thing was a last-minute choice," she wrote. "I was going to commit a school shooting at my old middle school but chose this instead. Although I didn’t commit a school shooting, the whole event was inspired by these people." She then listed the names of six different school shooters from memory. FATHER WHO BOUGHT AR-15 FOR GEORGIA SCHOOL SHOOTER LEARNS FATE IN FIRST-OF-ITS-KIND CONVICTION In the months before the killing, officials said Wagner communicated via apps with anonymous people who encouraged her to plan and commit murder. Investigators later found that Rachel Wagner had purchased the gun her daughter used at a pawn shop a month before the killing. She allowed the teen to keep the weapon and ammunition in her bedroom, prosecutors said. In a statement, Warren warned parents to monitor the content their children view online. FRANCE BECOMES FIRST EU NATION TO BAN SOCIAL MEDIA FOR CHILDREN UNDER 15 "I urge you to never underestimate the influence that exists behind your child’s screen," Warren said. "In the courtroom, I see the consequences after the messages and the online encouragement from strangers have already turned into real-world crimes." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "By then, remorse for your actions cannot erase the damage, and a prosecution cannot give victims back what was taken," Warren added. "It is your duty to know who is influencing your child, and it is your duty to know what they are being taught to believe is acceptable." Lilyana Wagner will serve 30 years in prison before becoming eligible for parole.

articles.title: Terrifying video captures people fleeing incoming mudslide at Nepal-China border
articles.summary: Video captures mudslides engulfing buildings in Gyirong, Tibet, minutes after a 4.4 magnitude earthquake triggered flash flooding near Nepal's border.
articles.body: A video taken after flash flooding on the border between Nepal and China shows mudslides enveloping multiple buildings as people fled in Gyirong, Tibet, near China's border with Nepal. The mudslides followed a 4.4-magnitude earthquake which occurred just seven minutes before video captured people sprinting away from the disaster, according to the German Research Centre for Geosciences (GFZ). Shishir Khanal, Nepal's foreign minister, also suggested that earthquakes could be the cause in remarks to the country's parliament, according to Reuters. COLOMBIA BUILDING COLLAPSES ON CAMERA AS EARTHQUAKE BRINGS DEATH, DESTRUCTION Authorities believe the earthquake caused an ice-rock avalanche that flowed into the Lhende Khola River in Nepal, according to Reuters. At least 95 people have been confirmed dead after rescue authorities in Nepal recovered at least that many bodies. Nepal's tourism authority said at least 484 tourists have also been reported missing, at least three of whom are U.S. citizens. Reports claim as many as several dozen more Americans are missing. No official count of Americans was immediately released by the U.S. government. The U.S. State Department said it was monitoring the situation closely and communicating with authorities in Nepal. "The Trump administration has no higher priority than the safety and security of Americans," a State Department spokesperson told Fox News Digital in a statement. "The State Department is aware of Americans impacted by the floods in Nepal and is closely tracking the situation. The embassy is working closely with local tour agencies and local authorities to assist Americans in the affected areas. We extend our deepest condolences for the victims and to the families of all those affected. "We strongly encourage U.S. citizens in the affected areas to monitor local news, follow the emergency instructions provided by local authorities, and enroll in STEP.state.gov to receive important emergency information," the spokesperson added. The State Department's office of Consular Affairs also relayed travel advisories for specific areas within Nepal. "The flood destroyed buildings and damaged roads, bridges, electricity infrastructure, and communications. Nepali authorities ordered people living along riverbanks and in low-lying areas to move to safer locations," the department posted on X. "Avoid travel on the Prithvi Highway, the Galchhi–Nuwakot–Rasuwa–Syafrubesi road, and the Mugling–Narayangadh road until authorities lift restrictions. If you are in Rasuwagadhi, Timure, Syafrubesi, Langtang, or another affected area, contact the U.S. Embassy when safe to do so and provide your name, location, and status," the advisory said. MORE THAN 3,000 MISSING AFTER COLOMBIA EARTHQUAKE AS TRUMP ADMINISTRATION PROVIDES $15.5 MILLION IN RELIEF Sixty-five people are being treated at hospitals in and around Nepal's capital of Kathmandu, according to local officials. Authorities also warned a second flood is possible since there is still a blockage on the Lhende Khola River. 33 RESCUED FROM VENEZUELAN RUBBLE: SURVIVAL WINDOW DESPERATELY FADING WITH NEARLY 50,000 MISSING China deployed 574 rescuers to Tibet's Gyirong land crossing, though one rescuer told CCTV it would take hours to reach the deluged site, Reuters reported. India's government and the European Union (EU) have publicly offered support to Nepal and China. US MILITARY DEPLOYS MTVRS, AIRLIFTS AID TO VENEZUELA FOLLOWING DEADLY EARTHQUAKES "Spoke to Prime Minister Balendra Shah and conveyed condolences on the loss of lives due to the floods in Nepal. The people of India stand in solidarity with their sisters and brothers in Nepal at this difficult time. India is ready to provide all possible humanitarian assistance to Nepal. Our teams are coordinating closely on rescue and relief efforts," Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi wrote in a post on X. Shah responded on X, calling Modi's gesture "a reflection of the enduring bonds of friendship between our two countries, which we profoundly value." "Devastating floods have struck communities in Nepal and China. My thoughts are with all those affected, especially the families who have lost loved ones or are still waiting for news... Copernicus has been activated to help map the affected areas in Nepal and support the response on the ground. We stand ready to mobilise further European assistance," European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen also wrote on X, offering up the use of Copernicus, the EU's Earth monitoring satellite program. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Fox News Digital also contacted Nepal's Ministry of Foreign Affairs for more information. Reuters contributed to this report.

articles.title: How to Clean a Dishwasher, According to Experts | NBC Selected
articles.summary: If you’ve ever thought about how to clean a dishwasher, this is the best way to do it. I talked to cleaning experts for their guidance and product recommendations.
articles.body: We don’t always have the answers, but we have some people on speed dial who do — which is why we present to you our series FYI where we have experts explain if hair removal cream is actually bad, how often you should change your towels and more. You probably clean your kitchen counters, stovetop and floors regularly — but you might not be able to say the same for your dishwasher. Dishwashers are great at clearing away remnants of dinners past from your dishes, but they may not be as clean as they appear. The dishwasher’s filter is a hotbed for food residue and soap scum, according to Kadi Dulude, owner of cleaning company Wizards of Homes. “When not removed in time, [debris] will clog the filter, food particles will start smelling bad and the machine won’t operate properly because it’s not draining anymore,” she says. The good news is cleaning a dishwasher doesn’t require expensive tools or special skills — just a little guidance. We consulted cleaning experts for their insight about the best way to clean a dishwasher, and for their recommendations of products to use to do it The best products for cleaning a dishwasher and more Before we get to the actual steps of how to clean a dishwasher, we’re sharing some products you may want to have on hand prior to starting the process. We rounded up products based on our experts’ recommendations and guidance. All of the products have at least a four-star average rating from 10,000 or more shoppers on Amazon. (with the exception of one that’s highly-rated but from fewer customers). This dishwasher detergent is meant to clean the inside of the dishwasher rather than the dishes themselves. I’ve previously used the Finish Quantum Powerball Dishwasher Pods, and they work better than any dishwasher pod I’ve ever used — on my dishes of course. In my experience, Finish’s products always do a great job of preventing residual water droplets from staying on surfaces. This liquid detergent comes in a square-shaped container that you place upside down in the bottom rack of the dishwasher. As you run a cycle with the container in it (and no dishes), let the detergent drain into the bottom of the dishwasher. It helps break down limescale and grease, and gets rid of odors, according to the brand. While you shouldn’t use regular liquid dish soap for cleaning dishes in a dishwasher, you can still use this multipurpose dish soap spray to handwash compartments within the dishwasher, such as the filter and spray arms. In fact, our experts commonly recommend using the dish spray for various projects, such as cleaning the refrigerator, and it’s one of our favorite soaps for hand washing dishes. This spray is thorough enough to get rid of grease and grime, according to the brand, but gentle enough to use on other surfaces without damaging them, like countertops. Plus, it doesn’t leave a strong chemical scent after you use it. Remove the filter from the dishwasher and, if possible, the spray arms. Spray with the soap and use a sponge or brush to scrub away grime. Then rinse and let them dry before putting the parts back in the dishwasher. A rinse aid, like this one from Cascade, will help your dishes dry faster after being cleaned in the dishwasher. It will also help get rid of hard water stains, which are very visible on things made out of glass. This dishwand is a great two-in-one gadget that combines the power of a dishwashing brush and a bottle of soap. The handle contains the dish soap, which dispenses from the end of the brush, underneath the bristles. This eliminates the need to constantly pour dish soap onto a sponge. You can fill the brush with your preferred dish soap and use the button on the top of the handle to control how much comes out. It’s typically meant to be used on dishes, but you can use it to hand wash the filter and spray arms of the dishwasher — simply rinse them off when you’re done and let them dry before putting them back into the dishwasher. Similar to Finish’s dishwasher cleaner, this bottle of detergent goes into the dishwasher upside down. All you have to do is let it dispense as the dishwasher runs. It removes limescale and mineral buildup, bacteria, grease and rust on the dishwasher filter, pipes and spray arms, according to the brand. For the best results, place it directly into the flatware basket in the bottom rack and run it on the hottest cycle once a month, according to the brand. The pack has three 12-ounce bottles with a lemon-scented formula inside. You can use one bottle to clean the dishwasher once a month, so one pack lasts three months. These cleaning brushes are great for cleaning reusable water bottles and straws, but they’re also good for cleaning the holes on the spray arms of a dishwasher. This set has brushes of varying sizes and thicknesses, so you can use the smaller ones to clean the sprinkler holes. The brushes are also dishwasher safe, so you can add them with a load of dishes after each use. What is the best way to clean a dishwasher? The best way to deep clean a dishwasher involves hand washing the different components of the machine, including the racks, filter and spray arms. I spoke with Ryan Knoll, the owner of cleaning company TidyCasa, for the best step-by-step way to clean a dishwasher. Here’s what he recommends: Remove the racks, spray arms and filter from the dishwasher. Use mild dish soap, a scrub brush and warm, soapy water to scrub them. If needed, use a toothbrush to scrub parts of the filter. Rinse the racks, spray arms and filter with water and set those aside. Wipe away any debris from the bottom of the dishwasher. With mild dish soap and a scrub brush, scrub the interior of the dishwasher with warm soapy water. Add the racks, spray arms and filter back into the dishwasher. Fill a dishwasher-safe measuring cup with one cup of distilled white vinegar and place it on the top rack of the dishwasher, making sure it’s sitting upright. Close the dishwasher and run it on the hottest cycle. Remove the vinegar after the cycle is complete and then run the dishwasher again. As an alternative to step three, use a dishwasher cleaner. Follow the instructions on the label. If you use the Finish Dishwasher Deep Cleaner or Glisten Dishwasher Cleaner, remove the top of the container, place the bottle upside down on the bottom rack or wherever it says in the directions and run the dishwasher on the hot water cycle. If you’re using a dishwasher cleaning tablet, then simply place it in the compartment before running the appliance. If it’s a stainless steel dishwasher, use a stainless steel cleaning spray and microfiber cloth or stainless steel cleaning wipe to clean the outside of the dishwasher door. Otherwise, use mild dish soap and a damp microfiber cloth to wipe the outside. Wipe away the residue with a dry microfiber cloth. How we picked the best products for cleaning a dishwasher Your dishwasher may appear clean on the outside, but many of its parts — such as the filter and spray arms — collect debris and minerals over time. Our experts recommend keeping the following tips in mind when looking for products to clean a dishwasher: Find specialized detergent: Dulude recommends against filling the detergent compartment of the dishwasher with regular liquid dish soap in general because it produces too much foam and suds. Instead use dishwasher detergents and/or tablets from brands like Finish, Affresh, Cascade and Glisten. These cleaners get rid of soap scum, food debris and limescale (residual minerals leftover from hard water), all of which are common causes of a smelly dishwasher. In fact, hard water residue buildup can decrease water pressure and affect the function of appliances, according to the United States Geological Survey. Go with acidic cleaning agents: You should also use acidic ingredients like distilled white vinegar to clean the inside of your dishwasher and its parts. That’s because the acidic nature of vinegar helps to lift and remove the stuck-on debris. Look for abrasive cleaning products: Abrasive ingredients and products, such as baking soda or a scrubbing brush, are ideal for cleaning parts of your dishwasher because they lift grime. Use a scratch-free sponge, dish brush or a Scrub Daddy. How to keep a dishwasher clean Once your dishwasher is clean, it’s important to maintain that cleanliness. Incorporating the simple steps below into your kitchen routine can help you stretch out the time between cleanings, which also saves you money on cleaners or ingredients in the long run. Pre-rinse dishes: Even though some brands may say that rinsing dishes before putting them in the dishwasher isn’t necessary to get them clean, it’s still a good idea to rinse them to prevent small particles of food from getting stuck in the filter. This also helps prevent rotting food smells from forming in your appliance.Unload dishes immediately: You should remove the dishes from the machine as soon as the cycle finishes. That’s because, even though the dishes are technically clean, they can develop water stains. Using a rinse aid can also prevent this. Use a rinse aid: Speaking of rinse aids, picks like Finish Jet-Dry Rinse Aid, help your dishes dry faster, which ultimately prevents them from developing hard water stains. articles.title: ICE arrests nearly 50,000 immigrants in July, highest monthly tally under Trump’s second term
articles.summary: US News: US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) arrested 49,571 people in July, marking the highest monthly arrest tally during President Donald Trump’s .
articles.body: US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) arrested 49,571 people in July, marking the highest monthly arrest tally during President Donald Trump’s second term, according to government data analysed by The Associated Press.The figure was 15 per cent higher than the 43,021 arrests recorded in June and about 70 per cent above February’s 29,241 arrests, the data showed. The numbers were provided by ICE to the Deportation Data Project at the University of California, Berkeley and UCLA.The surge comes as the Trump administration continues to pursue its mass deportation agenda, while shifting away from the highly visible immigration raids that drew widespread attention earlier in the year.Instead, enforcement has increasingly involved traffic stops, local police partnerships and arrests at routine immigration appointments.ICE’s expanding cooperation with state and local law enforcement accounted for about 6,500 arrests in July, or roughly 13% of the monthly total, according to the AP analysis. A year earlier, such partnerships made up less than 5 per cent of ICE arrests.Texas and Florida together accounted for nearly 20,000 arrests in July. Both states have expanded cooperation with ICE through 287(g) agreements, which allow local and state officers to perform certain immigration enforcement duties.The latest figures also indicate that a large share of those arrested did not have criminal convictions. More than half of the people arrested in July had neither been convicted of a crime nor faced criminal charges, while fewer than one-quarter had a criminal conviction, according to the data.Half of the arrests were non-custodial, meaning ICE agents apprehended people in their communities rather than taking them into custody after they had been held by local authorities.The increase follows a rise in arrests in June after the numbers had remained relatively flat for several months following a decline in February.Immigration arrests had been above 40,000 by December, after the administration loosened restrictions on where and whom ICE could arrest.The administration has also expanded the agency’s resources and staffing as it seeks to increase immigration enforcement.Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin had earlier indicated that the administration would pursue a quieter enforcement strategy, but the latest figures show that mass deportations remain a key priority.Immigration advocates and attorneys have reported arrests during traffic stops and other routine encounters, including cases involving people with valid work permits or pending asylum claims.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Key moments from Lindsay Clancy's five-week trial over children's killings
articles.summary: The trial often grew emotional as lawyers debated whether the mother was responsible for her children's deaths.
articles.body:
A panel of 12 jurors is expected to begin deliberations this week in the trial of Lindsay Clancy, the Massachusetts mother charged with murdering her three small children at their home in suburban Boston.

In a case that has captivated the American public, Clancy has not disputed that she killed them, but her lawyers argue she should not be held legally responsible because she was suffering from severe mental illness.

Clancy is charged with three counts of first-degree murder in the January 2023 deaths. If convicted, she faces life in prison without parole.

Here are some of the most notable moments in the emotional five-week trial.

Arguing a calculated decision to kill - or insanity

Prosecutors allege that on 24 January 2023, Clancy intentionally strangled all of her children - Cora, five, Dawson, three, and Callan, eight months - with fitness bands in their Duxbury, Massachusetts, home before jumping from a second-floor window. Clancy, now 36, was paralysed by the fall and attended the trial in a wheelchair.

Clancy's attorneys, while defending her, have never refuted her role in the killings.

Instead, they have put forth a defence of insanity, arguing that Clancy had hallucinations and delusions after giving birth to her youngest child. They pointed to treatment for mental health problems and that she checked herself into a psychiatric hospital just days before the deaths.

Prosecutors, meanwhile, have argued Clancy made a calculated decision to intentionally kill her children and should be held legally responsible. They allege that at the time, Clancy sent her husband, Patrick Clancy, out on errands so that he would not be home.

Clancy's family, including her former mother-in-law and husband, have all supported the theory, all testifying in her defence.

The five-week trial also sparked interest on social media as thousands watched the trial. Hundreds of women have showed up outside the courthouse to support Clancy, wearing pink shirts with phrases like "She Needed Help" and "Peace For Lindsay".

'A really hard time': Clancy's ex-husband takes stand

Over two days, Clancy's ex-husband, Patrick, told jurors about his ex-wife's declining mental health after giving birth and described the day his children died in gruesome detail.

He told jurors that Clancy's "big spiral" began about a month before their deaths.

"She started to lose a lot of weight, and she became very depressed, and she was having a really hard time," he said.

He described her intermittently seeking help from doctors and taking a variety of medications, adding that he recalled her saying she was starting to have thoughts of suicide.

Patrick Clancy described his last image of son Dawson sitting on the couch eating chicken nuggets before he left to get food and medication. He came back to find his children dead.

Lindsay Clancy sobbed in court as a recording of her husband's 911 call played. He can be heard screaming, "She killed the kids", after finding their children in the basement.

Since the beginning of the trial, conspiracy theories about Patrick Clancy have swirled online, including some speculating about his involvement. But he was never a suspect or under suspicion by investigators; Lindsay Clancy admitted to killing her children and her attorneys have not denied that.

Battles between lawyers and experts over Clancy's care

More than 10 expert witnesses testified for both the defence and the prosecution, including some who clashed with lawyers over Clancy's mental health.

Over the course of her treatment, Clancy was put on over a dozen medications, and sought help from a suicide hotline and the emergency room.

Clancy's team tried to convince jurors she had postpartum psychosis, a rare condition in which postpartum women can experience mania, depression or a mixture of both. Clancy claims she experienced hallucinations and delusions.

One day in the courtroom grew particularly heated as one of Clancy's psychiatrists, Jennifer Tufts, testified for the prosecution that Clancy did not show signs of psychosis during their sessions.

There were "no serious signs that her safety or anyone else's safety was at risk," said Tufts, who saw Clancy over a dozen times for five months.

But defence attorneys pointed to Tufts' medical notes, describing Clancy's "not hyper, pressured speech". Pressured speech - a rapid, frantic way of talking - can be a sign of mania.

Tufts denied that she believed Clancy had pressured speech, saying the "not" applied to both the words hyper and pressured. As defence attorney Kevin Reddington pressed her, she replied: "I don't care what it says. I know what I meant."

Reddington also grew tense as he repeatedly questioned another prosecution expert, psychiatrist Avram Mack, about whether postpartum psychosis is a diagnosis.

The American Psychiatric Association views postpartum psychosis as only a proposed illness, he said.

Mack avoided calling postpartum psychosis a recognised diagnosis, at one point responding: "I'm not sure if that specifically answers your question."

In a frustrated tone, Reddington responded: "I don't care."

In addition to Patrick Clancy, Lindsay's former mother-in-law, her mother and her sister also testified, telling jurors about Clancy's deteriorating mental health after the birth of her son.

Lindsay Clancy was "begging for help", her former mother-in-law Susan Clancy testified.

"She had insomnia. She was losing her appetite," she said. "She was very anxious and sad."

She added that Clancy had been a "very nurturing" mother until the birth of her youngest son.

Clancy's mother, Paula Musgrove, said her daughter told her and her ex-husband that she was having thoughts of harming the children a month before their deaths.

Musgrove said her daughter was becoming paranoid and expressed that she thought her medications were "destroying her mind".

Clancy's sister Allison Ozga told the court that her sister was experiencing suicidal thoughts every day a month before she killed her children.

Judge tells jurors to disregard testimony about Catholic faith

Two days before closing arguments, Clancy's defence team requested a mistrial after prosecutors asked witnesses about her Catholic faith.

Prosecutors last week asked Clancy's former mother-in-law, Susan Clancy, whether she was aware that murder was considered a "mortal sin" after asking her if she was Catholic, testimony that the judge asked jurors to disregard.

Then, this week, forensic psychologist Kirk Heilbrun, who interviewed Lindsay Clancy after the killings, testified that he had asked Clancy whether suicide was considered a "mortal sin" while discussing her Catholic upbringing.

Judge William Sullivan denied Clancy's legal team's request for a mistrial, but told jurors it was an "absolutely inappropriate area of testimony".

"It is to be stricken. It is not to be considered. I can't be any more clear of that," he said.

With additional reporting from Ana Faguy and Brandon Drenon

If you are suffering distress or despair and need support, you could speak to a health professional, or an organisation that offers support. Details of help available in many countries can be found at Befrienders Worldwide.

In the UK a list of organisations that can help is available at bbc.co.uk/actionline.

articles.title: Woman told 'nobody wants to see a pregnant person' in work
articles.summary: A sales manager from Swansea was told by a male colleague that "nobody wants to see a pregnant person".
articles.body:
A sales manager was discriminated against at work by being told "nobody wants to see a pregnant person" after she offered to make a presentation to clients.

Jessica Morgan was several months into her pregnancy when her boss at a wood panelling firm allegedly "sniggered" at her suggestion that she would lead the sales pitch.

A tribunal in Swansea heard that the boss at Panelex Wood, Frederick Geraint Hawkes, denied making the comment about her pregnancy.

It found that while Morgan's pregnancy and maternity discrimination claim had been "well-founded", it was dismissed because of the amount of time it had taken for her to bring it to them.

But another claim of victimisation did succeed.

The employment tribunal at Swansea Magistrates' Court was told in May that Morgan had joined the firm in Fforestfach, on the outskirts of Swansea, in 2020, for her £40,000-a-year sales role and that she had announced her pregnancy in July 2023.

In a written judgment issued in June 2026, the tribunal said Morgan had felt that Hawkes's demeanour had changed towards her and that she had a sense that her pregnancy was "an inconvenience".

The tribunal found that Morgan had been unable to give specific examples of why she felt this and had been "largely perceived by the claimant because of her own anxiety".

The tribunal said it heard that Morgan and Hawkes had a "strong working and personal relationship" and were the only two members of staff in the office full-time, with Morgan reporting to him.

"There was, we find, a power imbalance between them that went beyond the obvious power imbalance of employer/employee," the tribunal said, noting that Morgan had been "somewhat reliant on Hawkes and sought his approval".

Morgan had claimed that around November 2023, before she had gone on maternity leave, she offered to assist Hawkes in preparing for a presentation for a client, and that he responded "nobody wants to see a pregnant woman, Jess".

Hawkes denied making the comment while giving evidence, and pointed to the inconsistency in when Morgan said it had been made, but the tribunal decided that he had.

Morgan started her maternity leave in January 2024, and later left the firm around October that year following a meeting with Hawkes.

The tribunal said it found that both parties had agreed she would not return to work, despite Morgan's claim that she had felt she was "persuaded" to reach the agreement.

Morgan's other claims of unfair dismissal, wrongful dismissal and sex discrimination against her employer were all dismissed.

The tribunal found that Hawkes's comment about Morgan's pregnancy amounted to "unfavourable treatment", and suggested "that the way a pregnant woman looks will make her off-putting to clients to the extent that she should not be seen".

But despite the claim being well-founded, the amount of time it had taken for Morgan to bring it meant it had been "significantly out of time".

"The claim is dismissed because the tribunal lacks jurisdiction to consider it," the tribunal said.

Morgan succeeded in a claim of victimisation, after the tribunal found she was sent an "aggressive and threatening" letter in which Hawkes had reneged on an agreement for Morgan to keep a company car until Christmas 2024.

It had been sent after she asked to be paid in lieu of holiday entitlement she had accrued during her maternity leave.

Another hearing will be held to decide if any compensation will be awarded.

articles.title: US imposes sanctions on Palestine Action and other left-wing groups
articles.summary: Palestine Action’s Huda Ammori says Trump’s penalties should be a ‘wake-up call’ for UK to lift ban on the group.
articles.body:
The United States has imposed sanctions on the British activist group Palestine Action and the pro-Palestine international movement Masar Badil as the administration of President Donald Trump intensifies a global crackdown on critics of Israel.

The US Department of the Treasury also imposed financial penalties on Wednesday against Autistici Inventati, an Italy-based group that provides digital services to left-wing organisations, including pro-Palestine groups.

Palestine Action, which has been locked in a legal battle with the United Kingdom after the British government proscribed it as a “terrorist” group, rejected the US sanctions.

Palestine Action cofounder Huda Ammori linked the US measures to the UK designation and called on Prime Minister Andy Burnham to reverse the ban on the group imposed by his predecessor Keir Starmer.

“The fact that Trump is now taking inspiration from Britain’s repression of the movement for Palestinian freedom exposes just how dangerous this ban is and should be a wake-up call to anyone who cares about free speech and civil liberties,” Ammori told Al Jazeera in a statement.

“By banning a direct action protest group under terrorism legislation for the first time in British history, Keir Starmer’s Government has created a blueprint for authoritarian governments around the world to suppress political dissent, and to criminalise British citizens who travel or live abroad.”

The UK civil rights group Defend Our Juries echoed Ammori’s comment.

“We’ve warned since July 2025 that Keir Starmer’s unprecedented ban on Palestine Action would embolden autocrats and demagogues around the world. Today that warning has proved to be well-founded,” it said. “Whilst bowing down to the arms industry and Israel lobby, the UK government has encouraged Trump to escalate his domestic crackdown on civil liberties.”

Palestine Action says it uses direct-action tactics, including vandalism, to end what it sees as complicity in Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza.

While such protests could break the law, rights advocates have argued that the “terrorism” designation is disproportionate and risks chilling free speech.

The UK has arrested thousands of people for showing support for Palestine Action since the group was proscribed last year.

A British court revoked the designation in February, but the decision was overturned on appeal in June.

Palestine Action has continued to challenge the ban, taking the case to the UK Supreme Court.

The Trump administration framed Wednesday’s sanctions as part of a push against what it called “far-left terrorist groups”.

“Far-left extremists, their fronts, and their enablers should be on notice: We will bring the full weight of our economic tools to bear,” Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in a statement. “Political terrorism has no place in our society, and we will continue to cut the financial lifelines of these groups until they are eliminated.”

The sanctions freeze the groups’ assets in the US and make it generally illegal for American citizens to engage in financial transactions with them.

The US has been relying on sanctions to punish supporters of Palestinian rights across the world. Last year, the Trump administration imposed penalties on United Nations rapporteur Francesca Albanese .

Washington has also sanctioned International Criminal Court officials, including the tribunal’s president, Tomoko Akane.

articles.title: Man convicted in murder-for-hire killing of Microsoft manager on Florida road
articles.summary: JACKSONVILLE, Fla. — A man accused of arranging the fatal shooting of a Microsoft design manager on a Florida road was convicted Wednesday in a murder-for-hire scheme fueled by a stormy child custody arrangement between the victim and his wealthy ex-wife.
articles.body: JACKSONVILLE, Fla. — A man accused of arranging the fatal shooting of a Microsoft design manager on a Florida road was convicted Wednesday in a murder-for-hire scheme fueled by a stormy child custody arrangement between the victim and his wealthy ex-wife. Jared Bridegan was shot four years ago after he got out of his SUV to remove a tire from a road in Jacksonville Beach. The attack stumped police for months as they struggled to understand why someone with no apparent enemies would be killed while his daughter sat nearby in her car seat. Prosecutors believe he was killed because of ongoing strife with his former wife over the parenting of their twins. Mario Fernandez Saldana, 38, was convicted of first-degree murder and solicitation of murder. He’s married to Bridegan’s former wife, Shanna Gardner, whose trial is set to start in September. Bridegan was “unarmed, unaware, exposed, vulnerable. He couldn’t have known, on that cold asphalt in February of 2022, the architects of his murder had been making preparations for his death for months,” Assistant State Attorney Christina Stifler said during closing arguments. Defense attorney Jesse Dreicer told jurors that Fernandez Saldana had no motive to have Bridegan killed. Fernandez Saldana and Gardner are estranged, and Gardner moved to Washington state after the killing. “He certainly gained no benefit from the death of Jared Bridegan,” Dreicer said, noting there was no testimony that Fernandez Saldana told anyone that Bridegan “deserves to die.” The alleged gunman, Henry Tenon, had no personal connection to Bridegan, but he was a former tenant at Fernandez Saldana’s rental property in Jacksonville. Jurors saw three checks totaling $10,000 written to Tenon after the homicide, marked as payments for handyman work and a business idea. Tenon’s DNA was identified on the rim of the tire that was intentionally placed in the road, police said. Tenon, 65, initially pleaded guilty and agreed to testify against Fernandez Saldana, but he later backed out of the deal and will stand trial next year. Gardner, 39, is the daughter of the co-founder of Stampin’ Up!, an arts-and-crafts company based in Utah. Bridegan was shot twice when he stopped his Volkswagen Atlas to remove a tire from the road. He had just returned two children to Gardner’s home after a “date night” meal with the twins. At the time of his death, he was married to Kirsten Bridegan and they had two children. Kirsten Bridegan told the jury that the post-divorce relationship between her husband and Gardner was “pretty terrible,” adding there was “absolutely no trust.”

articles.title: NASA, Fed, Senate among Chinese hackers’ targets, Justice Department says
articles.summary: The Department of Justice (DOJ) announced Wednesday that it disrupted a Chinese hacking operation that targeted its network and other sensitive U.S. agencies. The DOJ said in a statement that it seized hacking platforms “QScan” and “QTRouter,” which were operated by a state-run group employed by Chinese-based firm, Nanjing Xinjiuwei Network Technology Co. These platforms…
articles.body:
The Department of Justice (DOJ) announced Wednesday that it disrupted a Chinese hacking operation that targeted its network and other sensitive U.S. agencies.

The DOJ said in a statement that it seized hacking platforms “QScan” and “QTRouter,” which were operated by a state-run group employed by Chinese-based firm, Nanjing Xinjiuwei Network Technology Co.

These platforms worked in tandem to “target U.S. critical infrastructure and other sensitive networks” for clients like the Ministry of State Security and the People’s Liberation Army, according to the DOJ release.

This hacking operation targeted the DOJ, NASA, the Federal Reserve, the Department of Energy, the U.S. Senate, the Department of Health and Human Services and the National Institutes of Health, according to a court affidavit unsealed in the Southern District of California.

Other reported targets included government contractors, hospital networks, telecommunications providers, power companies and financial institutions.

“State-sponsored malicious hackers preying on America’s critical infrastructure will be stopped and prosecuted,” Attorney General Todd Blanche said in a statement. “We are here to ensure security for the American people and will use every tool we have to keep that promise.”

The affidavit said the Chinese firm’s infrastructure has been used to “compromise critical infrastructure and other sensitive networks” in the U.S. and around the globe since 2018.

The Hill has reached out to the Chinese Embassy in Washington, D.C., for comment. The Chinese government routinely denies allegations of hacking U.S. networks.

In a separate hacking operation announced by the Treasury Department in 2024, the department charged 10 Chinese hackers-for-hire and two of the country’s officials in a scheme to steal data from American entities.

FBI Director Kash Patel thanked the joint work of the FBI and the bureau’s San Diego office and cyber division on the seizure operation in a Wednesday statement.

“Today’s action is just the latest technical operation against PRC-sponsored hacking – and in support of President Trump’s Cyber Strategy for America, the FBI is surging efforts to shape adversary behavior and defend the homeland in cyberspace,” Patel said.

The announcement comes ahead of Chinese leader Xi Jinping’s scheduled visit to the U.S. next month, during which he will meet with President Trump.

When asked Wednesday on Fox News about whether this hacking scheme would come up between the two leaders, Blanche said he would not “tell President Trump what he needs to talk to the leadership about in China.”

“This is something that we’ve talked about with our counterparts in China for many, many years,” Blanche said. “And we know that it’s happening. And they know we know that it’s happening. And it has to stop.”

articles.title: Kurdish-led SDF has dissolved, but has Syria really unified its military?
articles.summary: SDF’s dissolution is a major victory for Damascus, but unresolved questions over command and deployment remain.
articles.body:
Tuesday’s announcement that the Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces had dissolved , with its forces merging with the Syrian military, represents a boost for a government seeking to demonstrate that it has sole authority over the country.

And yet, analysts have told Al Jazeera, the finer details of military integration remain, indicating that the divisions that have beset Syria over almost 14 years of war, and then in the 20 months since the fall of the al-Assad regime, have not been totally eradicated.

The SDF, which emerged in 2015, has been based in the country’s northeast, where much of Syria’s historically marginalised Kurdish population lives.

Despite months of talks, the SDF had been unwilling to give up on the autonomy it had gained during Syria’s war, but on Tuesday the group’s leader Mazloum Abdi (also known as Mazloum Kobani) said that an “important page” had been turned in the country’s history.

“We want this day to be the beginning of a true transition from the battlefields to the fields of construction, and from the era of weapons to the era of peace,” Abdi said from the presidential palace in Damascus.

Initially, the SDF had held strong reservations over giving up its arms and coming under the command of Syria’s Ministry of Defence. But a government-led offensive into the northeast in January, in addition to good relations between the Syrian government and the United States – the SDF’s main backer – has shifted the balance of power.

Rob Geist Pinfold, a lecturer on security studies at King’s College London, told Al Jazeera that the SDF’s dissolution “is part of an ongoing trend of the SDF losing its leverage in Syria, simply because the US has signalled that [the SDF] no longer has protected status from the US”.

The SDF’s dissolution means that “the largest organised military force outside Damascus’s authority has ended its independent existence, allowing the state to begin the process of restoring a single military command and unified control over the border, airports, and strategic resources”, said Navvar Saban, a researcher in security and military affairs at the Arab Center for Contemporary Syrian Studies.

But, Saban added, the process of integration will take more than an announcement in Damascus.

“The agreement may end Syria’s military division, but inclusive institutions and a single national chain of command are what will make the unity sustainable and effective,” Saban said.

Saban said that SDF military fighters are being incorporated into the Syrian army under the command of the Defence Ministry, while the Asayish – the SDF’s affiliated security forces – and other local security bodies are being integrated into the Ministry of Interior. Civilian institutions and employees are also being transferred to relevant ministries.

“The formal merge has been completed, but creating a unified military culture and chain of command will take much longer,” he said.

There is also likely to be some apprehension from Syrian Kurds, with a deadly war still recent in their memories, and some mistrust towards Syria’s government. The government is led by figures formerly associated with now-disbanded rebel groups, including Hay’at Tahrir al-Sham, whose predecessor, al-Nusra Front, was once affiliated with al-Qaeda. Many of the former rebel groups had also fought the SDF, which was accused of cooperating with the al-Assad regime at times.

“Many Arab communities may welcome the return of the central institution [government], while Kurdish communities are likely to be more cautious,” Saban said. “They want peace. But they also need guarantees concerning the Kurdish language, education, political representation, and local security.”

Syria’s President Ahmed al-Sharaa has made efforts since assuming power in the wake of al-Assad’s fall to assuage Kurdish concerns, repeatedly pledging constitutional protection for Kurdish language and political rights, but insisting on integration into the wider Syrian state.

“This is an agreement that comes on the government’s terms, but it’s likely that US pressure behind the scenes meant that the [Syrian government] capitulated to at least some of the remaining demands from the SDF,” Geist Pinfold said.

There have been particular disagreements over the SDF’s Women Protection Units, also known as the YPJ. Earlier this month, SDF senior official Abdulkarim Omar told Al Jazeera that the YPJ wanted to join the Defence Ministry, but had instead been told by the Syrian government that the army’s existing structure did not include units for women.

The government had instead suggested the YPJ be integrated into the Interior Ministry. Omar said that the YPJ had countered that it could join the Interior Ministry as a specialised counterterrorism unit.

No final decision has been announced, but Alexander McKeever, author of the newsletter This Week in Northern Syria, said that this represented “a significant compromise for the government”, which had previously rejected women in combat or heavy security roles.

However, McKeever, speaking from Qamishli in northeast Syria, said that there were still general disagreements over the larger integration process, including which fighters would join government forces, where they would be deployed, and what their roles would be.

McKeever said the question of chain of command – whether fighters will directly report to Damascus or to more local command – is still unanswered.

articles.title: Nearly 100 dead, hundreds missing in Nepal-China flood catastrophe
articles.summary: The death toll from severe flash floods in the mountainous border region between Nepal and China rose to nearly 100 late Wednesday, with hundreds of people s...
articles.body:
The death toll from severe flash floods in the mountainous border region between Nepal and China rose to nearly 100 late Wednesday, with hundreds of people still missing and fears that the true number could run into the thousands.

The office of Nepalese Prime Minister Balendra Shah said at least 95 people had died in the country. Hundreds remained unaccounted for, including 391 foreign tourists, 93 Nepalese travellers, 44 Nepal Army personnel and 31 police officers.

A senior official at Nepal Police headquarters in Kathmandu, speaking to dpa on condition of anonymity because of sensitivity of the matter, said the number of missing could be "in the thousands" based on preliminary assessment, though complete data is still being gathered.

"Gathering complete information itself is challenging as many areas remained cut off from communication and roads throughout the day," the officer said.

The floods caused widespread destruction to communities and infrastructure along the Bhotekoshi river, which originates in the highlands of the Tibet Autonomous Region of China and flows through Nepal's Bagmati province.

Television footage and videos shared on social media showed homes, hydropower facilities and roads destroyed, bridges swept away and entire villages inundated, with the Rasuwa district hardest hit. Surveillance footage showed a border crossing with China being wiped out by a massive wave of water and mud.

What triggered the catastrophe remains unclear. Authorities have not ruled out a glacial lake outburst, in which a lake fed by melting glaciers suddenly releases a massive volume of water after becoming destabilized, unleashing huge volumes of water downstream.

The floods destroyed at least 19 road bridges and around 40 kilometres of paved roads, according to updated figures from the Nepalese government.

The Nepal Tourism Board said earlier that most of the missing travellers were from neighbouring India, citing preliminary figures from travel and trekking agencies operating tours in the affected region.

The army and other security forces would be deployed in rescue operations.

China reported three deaths and 265 people missing in Gyirong county in south-western Tibet, according to state media, citing an initial assessment by local authorities. The exact number of missing people was still being determined and rescue operations were continuing.

The mud and floodwaters cut roads leading to the border crossing as well as electricity supplies and communications, China's state-run Xinhua news agency reported.

China dispatched rescue teams with heavy equipment to the area, raised its disaster alert level and allocated emergency funds to the affected region.

Chinese President Xi Jinping called for all-out efforts to find the missing and move people in affected areas to safety, according to Xinhua. He also called for stronger early-warning systems and sent senior Communist Party official Zhang Guoqing to the region to oversee rescue efforts.

articles.title: King Charles’ royal soldiers honor Dolly with ‘9 to 5’ performance
articles.summary: The band performed the song during the Changing of the Guard ceremony.
articles.body:
( NewsNation ) — King Charles’ soldiers honored Dolly Parton with a performance of her hit song “9 to 5” in front of Buckingham Palace.

The country music legend died Tuesday at the age of 80, after what was described as a brief battle with cancer .

The following morning, the royal family shared a video on Instagram of the Band of the Coldstream Guards playing the 1980 classic during the Changing of the Guard ceremony.

“Remembering the late, great Dolly, who brought joy, comfort and inspiration to so many – including the millions of children given free books through her Imagination Library,” the caption reads.

Parton’s Imagination Library is a global program that sends free books to preschool-age children each month to foster a love of reading. Parton started the program to honor her father, who never learned to read or write, and to help children growing up in poverty as she had.

Following the “Jolene” singer’s death, tributes have poured in from fellow musicians, celebrities and fans who have celebrated her legacy .

In 1977, Parton appeared at the Royal Variety Performance for Queen Elizabeth II’s Silver Jubilee, meeting the late monarch, who she described as very warm and sweet.

After turning down an invitation for tea from Kate Middleton, the Princess of Wales, because she was busy promoting an album, Parton invited the princess, Prince William and their children, Prince George, Princess Charlotte and Prince Louis, to visit her Dollywood theme park , though it does not appear they took her up on the offer.

In 2025, she told HuffPost of plans to meet the royals, citing the royal family’s involvement with the Imagination Library.

Josh Gottheimer, D-N.J.; Ritchie Torres, D-N.Y.; Jared Moskowitz, D-Fla.; Brad Schneider, D-Ill.; Greg Stanton, D-Ariz.; and Hillary Scholten, D-Mich. articles.title: Mystery Turkish firm ordered by council to tear down holiday homes built without planning permission after hundreds of trees cut down in 500-year-old woodland, 100 ordered to replace those lost
articles.summary: UK News: A mysterious Turkish firm has been ordered to undo major changes made to an ancient woodland in West Yorkshire after a planning inspector found that m.
articles.body: A mysterious Turkish firm has been ordered to undo major changes made to an ancient woodland in West Yorkshire after a planning inspector found that much of the development could not remain on the site.According to SWNS, Azara Gid San, an agricultural company from Turkey, bought the 33-acre Jacobs Farm in Silsden, Keighley, for £1.05 million two years ago. The site later became the centre of a planning dispute after hundreds of trees were allegedly removed and several buildings and other structures were constructed without planning permission.Following a three-day inquiry in July, Planning Inspector Paul Hocking rejected the company's appeal against Bradford Metropolitan District Council's enforcement notice.Holiday homes and concrete structures ordered to be removedThe inspector upheld the enforcement action covering two newly erected buildings, three concrete pads and associated septic tanks.The order also requires the removal of fixtures, fittings and pipes connected to the structures, along with the excavated areas where the septic tanks were installed.Stockpiled earth and aggregate must also be cleared from the land, while materials imported to create an access track must be removed.The work has to be completed within 12 calendar months, according to the appeal decision.Two holiday homes were excluded from the enforcement action after the inspector found they had been built outside the relevant time period.100 trees must be planted to replace those lostThe case also focused heavily on the loss of trees from the woodland.Bradford Council had originally demanded that 300 trees be planted to compensate for the loss and that the site be restored to its previous condition.Inspector Hocking, however, ordered 100 replacement trees to be planted within 20 months. The planting is expected to include oak, silver birch, field maple, rowan, crab apple, hazel and hawthorn.He also rejected the suggestion that some of the trees had been lost or damaged because of a landslide.The developer has additionally been ordered to pay Bradford Council significant costs following the unsuccessful appeal.Firm claimed work was done before it bought the landAzara Gid San had described itself as an "innocent party", arguing that the disputed works had largely been carried out before it purchased Jacobs Farm.The company claimed the development had been completed more than four years earlier and had therefore become immune from enforcement because of the passage of time.That argument was rejected following the inquiry.In its appeal, the company also argued that the buildings were being used as holiday accommodation and would complement existing permitted holiday lets on the site.It claimed the development would support the local economy and pointed to increased demand for holiday accommodation in the region following Bradford's year as UK City of Culture in 2025.Ancient woodland described as irreplaceableThe dispute has caused particular concern because of the ecological importance of Jacobs Farm.The woodland is believed to be more than 500 years old and contains rich ground flora considered important for wildlife. It also provides habitat for protected species, including bats and breeding birds.Wildlife groups raised concerns about the impact of the tree clearance and construction.Penny Hunt, co-founder of Yorkshire Dales Wildlife Rescue, said, "Ancient woodlands are incredibly special and are absolutely irreplaceable."Bradford Council said the unauthorised works had harmed the openness of the green belt and diminished the appearance of the Airedale landscape.The site is also within the zone of influence of the South Pennine Moors Special Protection Area.Enforcement action began in 2025The latest decision follows a Temporary Stop Notice issued by Bradford Council in September 2025 after officials became aware of unauthorised development at the site.The council subsequently issued its enforcement notice in January, alleging that five large concrete pads had been created, four of which had holiday homes built on them. It also cited four septic tanks, an access track and stockpiled earth and aggregate.The planning dispute eventually went before the Planning Inspectorate, resulting in the three-day inquiry in July.What is known about the Turkish company?Azara Gid San is understood to be involved in production and export activities in Turkey, including food products such as olive oil and spices.Property records show that Jacobs Wood Farm was sold two years ago for £1.05 million. The property's description mentioned three other properties on the land but did not detail the works that later became the subject of the enforcement case.Sam Dewar, director of Dewar Planning Associates, who represented the appellant, had previously argued that the council's enforcement action was not justified."We accept that the alleged buildings and hardstanding were built without planning, but our understanding is that they were completed prior to my client's purchase, albeit apart from the forestry maintenance building," Dewar said.He also described the council's actions as "extremely disappointing" and claimed officials had been "very aggressive".The company had previously said it was willing to reach a suitable solution with the council, although it claimed the authority had not been forthcoming.With the appeal now dismissed, the developer faces a substantial restoration bill and a deadline to remove much of the unauthorised development from the ancient woodland.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Hundreds of volunteers pull 360-tonne historic Japanese castle back into place by hand
articles.summary: About 1,800 volunteers pulled ropes to move the 360-tonne Hirosaki Castle keep back into position using hikiya, an ancient Japanese moving technique.
articles.body: Japan enlisted the help of hundreds of volunteers to move a portion of a 360-tonne castle more than six feet back into position, inch by inch, following renovations to the structure. About 1,800 people gathered over the weekend to pull large ropes attached to the Hirosaki Castle keep in Aomori Prefecture, The Independent reported. The keep — which is a fortified tower within a castle — was moved so repairs could be completed on a wall damaged during a major earthquake. The wall has since been rebuilt, with all 2,185 stones returned to their original positions. JAPAN MALL REBUILT AFTER DEADLY 2016 EARTHQUAKE DESTROYED IN MAJOR TEMBLOR WEEKS AFTER 'FRESH START' REOPENING Rotating teams used an ancient technique known as hikiya, in which buildings are placed on rollers or rails and moved intact. The technique is used to preserve historic Japanese buildings that might otherwise be damaged or destroyed. "We had about 8,000 applications for the 1,800 slots over the last two days, roughly four times oversubscribed, so not everyone could participate," Kensuke Hayasaka, head of the parks and green spaces division in Hirosaki City, told The Guardian. "Not only from the city, but from across Japan and overseas; a fair number from Southeast Asia, Europe and North America." MASSIVE 7.7-MAGNITUDE EARTHQUAKE HITS OFF JAPANESE COAST Pulling the castle keep by hand will continue through the end of August, with about 4,100 people scheduled to move it a total of more than 16 feet, The Guardian reported. The Hirosaki Castle keep was originally a five-story tower, but it was destroyed by a lightning strike in 1627, the newspaper reported, citing the Japan National Tourism Organization. articles.title: German airport workers die from malaria caught from plane-riding mosquito
articles.summary: Four infected employees being treated in hospital; mosquito traps deployed at Frankfurt hub.
articles.body:
Two Frankfurt airport workers have died after contracting malaria from a mosquito believed to have hitched a ride on an incoming flight, according to the city’s health authority.

Airport officials had initially reported one death among six infected employees. The toll rose to two on Wednesday.

Germany’s Robert Koch Institute (RKI) points to an imported Anopheles mosquito, likely carried in on an aircraft, as the most likely source of the infection.

Malaria cases are rare in Germany. The RKI says the country’s last airport-linked malaria outbreak was in 2023.

The institute added that the rarity can, however, work against patients, since doctors may not immediately suspect the disease, which delays diagnosis and raises risks of severe illness.

The remaining four infected employees are being treated in hospital, an airport spokesman said, adding that mosquito traps have now been installed on site.

The mosquitoes caught will be transferred to the Institute of Tropical Medicine in Antwerp, Belgium for genetic tests to find out more about their origin.

Malaria is a serious, mosquito-borne infectious disease caused by microscopic parasites. It is spread through Anopheles mosquitoes and can cause symptoms such as nausea, headache and intense waves of fever and chills. The disease causes hundreds of thousands of deaths a year, mostly in sub-Saharan Africa.

There are treatments if infected patients detect the disease early enough, and they usually make a complete recovery.

articles.title: UNRWA chief condemns Israeli seizure of East Jerusalem facility
articles.summary: Christian Saunders tells Al Jazeera raid part of campaign to weaken agency and eliminate Palestinian rights.
articles.body:
The head of the UN agency for Palestinian refugees (UNRWA) has condemned an Israeli seizure of its East Jerusalem training centre, calling the raid part of a campaign designed to weaken the agency and, in turn, eliminate Palestinian rights.

In comments to Al Jazeera, acting Commissioner-General Christian Saunders on Wednesday accused Israel of violating UN premises, but insisted that “might doesn’t win out” in resolving the conflict and that the agency is “not going anywhere”.

Israeli forces raided and seized the Qalandiya Training Centre in the Kafr Aqab neighbourhood on Tuesday, expelling UNRWA employees and ordering them not to return.

Five Palestinians were injured by Israeli gunfire near the site, according to the Jerusalem governorate.

Far-right Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir took part in the raid and said there was “no place for the agency in Jerusalem and Israel”. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the evacuation was lawful and carried out under legislation passed by Israel.

The takeover of the facility deprives hundreds of young Palestinians of education and violates the protections afforded to UN premises under international law, Saunders said.

“Three hundred and forty young people are not going to get the education, not going to get the training they need,” he remarked. He lamented that the students – mostly from disadvantaged families – will now miss out on learning the skills to give them the “opportunity to lead a full and dignified life”.

The Qalandiya centre is part of UNRWA’s wider network of services for Palestinian refugees. It serves about 16,000 refugees from Qalandiya refugee camp and other parts of the occupied West Bank.

The raid followed the closure of the nearby Qalandiya checkpoint and a heavy Israeli military deployment in the area.

Israeli authorities said the property was owned by the Jewish National Fund and has now been allocated to the Jerusalem Municipality for a planned educational and community complex. They also cited Israeli legislation, passed in October 2024, restricting UNRWA’s activities.

UNRWA rejected the claims and maintained that the centre is a United Nations facility protected under international law.

UNRWA has come under severe pressure amid Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza and abuse in the occupied West Bank, with several workers having been killed.

Saunders said the wider campaign against UNRWA is intended to weaken the agency and cut its funding, and links these efforts to the broader question of Palestinian refugee rights.

“If UNRWA is defunded and UNRWA is eliminated then they are hoping that the issue of the refugees, the Palestine refugees, will go away,” Saunders said. “Which means that the right of return, reparations, and compensation would go away, as well.”

The aid group chief pointed out that its mandate comes directly from the United Nations General Assembly and its role is to provide humanitarian and public services while the wider political dispute between Israel and Palestinians remains unresolved.

“We’re a humanitarian organisation; we’re a development organisation. We are given our mandate by the United Nations General Assembly to provide critical services,” Saunders said.

UNRWA will continue doing so “until the General Assembly decides otherwise, or there is a durable solution to the Palestine question,” he declared.

However, Saunders also acknowledged the limits of the UN’s ability to prevent further incursions without collective action from member states.

“I don’t think the United Nations has the power to say: ‘You know, this is not going to continue to happen,’” he said.

“The United Nations is the sum of its member states, and its member states need to have the collective determination to address this issue. And for over seven decades, this has not happened.”

articles.title: Scientists discover a huge freshwater reservoir beneath the Great Salt Lake in Utah with the help of air drones
articles.summary: US News: A large freshwater reservoir appears to be hiding beneath the eastern edge of Utah’s Great Salt Lake, according to a 2026 study published in Scientifi.
articles.body: A large freshwater reservoir appears to be hiding beneath the eastern edge of Utah’s Great Salt Lake, according to a 2026 study published in Scientific Reports. Researchers used an airborne electromagnetic survey to look beneath the lake’s salty surface. They found a broad layer that behaves differently from the brine above it. The findings suggest that freshwater-saturated sediments extend across part of the Farmington Bay Playa and may continue into a much deeper basin beneath the lake. The study is important because the discovery could reveal a difficult-to-map water resource beneath one of North America’s best-known saline lakes. It also offers a new way to understand the hidden groundwater system beneath the lake. It is important as scientists seek better ways to manage the region’s water and understand the environmental pressures facing the Great Salt Lake today.Discovering freshwater under Utah’s Great Salt Lake without even drillingThe discovery came from a pilot airborne survey carried out over part of the Great Salt Lake in Utah. The research team wanted to determine whether freshwater existed below the lake’s highly saline surface and, if so, how far it extended. According to the study, researchers used airborne electromagnetic(AEM) technology to measure changes in the electrical properties beneath the lake. The technique allowed them to distinguish between the highly conductive salty water near the surface and a much less conductive layer underneath. The survey covered 248 kilometres of flight lines across the Farmington Bay Project Area during five flights in a single day. Rather than drilling across the lake, the researchers were able to build a 3D picture of the underground environment from measurements collected from the air. The results showed a broad, resistive layer beneath the saline material. While such a signal can have several possible causes, the researchers had an important advantage of confirmed freshwater-saturated sediments in the same area. That meant the airborne results provided evidence not simply of an unusual underground feature, but of the wider continuation of a known freshwater system.How large and deep could the hidden water system beThe survey revealed that freshwater-saturated sediments continue laterally beneath the southeastern part of the lake, particularly beneath the Farmington Bay Playa. Beneath the area, the rocky basement changes dramatically in depth. In one part, the basement lies less than 200 metres below the surface. Further west, it drops sharply, reaching depths of more than 3 kilometres. The researchers interpret this deeper basin as potentially containing freshwater-saturated sediments. If that interpretation is correct, the underground system could hold a substantial volume of freshwater. However, the study does not present the entire deep basin as a confirmed freshwater reservoir. The researchers stress that additional hydrological observations are needed to test the interpretation.Reason for the existence of freshwater beneath the Great Salt Lake.The study explains that the area was once covered by freshwater Lake Bonneville, which existed around 15,000 years ago. As the climate changed, the ancient lake declined and became increasingly salty, eventually giving rise to the modern Great Salt Lake. Groundwater continues to move through the region. The Wasatch Mountains east of the lake receive significant precipitation, allowing groundwater to recharge before moving westwards towards the lake and its surrounding playas. This helps explain how freshwater can exist beneath a lake that is now famously saline. The modern surface environment and the deeper groundwater system are not the same. Beneath the salty water and sediments, older and continuing groundwater movement can create a very different underground environment.What is the next step of exploration in the basinThe researchers describe the survey as a pilot project rather than a complete examination of the Great Salt Lake. Only a limited portion of the lake was surveyed, meaning the findings cannot yet be applied automatically to the entire basin. The scientists say a lake-wide airborne survey would be needed to establish how continuous the freshwater sediments are, determine their thickness and identify changes across the wider lakebed. Such a survey could also help identify areas where groundwater enters or leaves the underground system and improve understanding of the boundary between freshwater and saltwater. The study shows that airborne electromagnetic surveys can cover large areas quickly, making them useful for investigating the more than 4,000-square-kilometre footprint of the Great Salt Lake. For now, the discovery represents a glimpse into a largely unseen world beneath the Great Salt Lake.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
